source.title: SuperAI: Merging Capabilities Across Heterogeneous Foundation Models
source.authors: Jing-Tong Dou; Chuan-Cheng Shi; Wen-Hua Wu; Wei Bao; Fei Shen; Zhi-Yong Wang; T. Chua

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some equations, figures, and table layout are flattened or visually garbled, but the alignment results used here are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model representation alignment using shared prompts, PCA, and orthogonal Procrustes mappings. This bears on whether representations can be aligned with a simple map, but it does not reproduce the original studies’ convergence measurements or test alignment increasing with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports alignment diagnostics for task-relevant language-model representations, including Match, CKA, and Retrieval@1, and reports alignment scores for layer-pair conditions. The cited Platonic Representation Hypothesis is background, not a result of this study. The paper does not measure alignment as a function of model scale or capability, test paired image-caption representations, compare training seeds for shared features, or identify recurring interpretable features. Capability-fusion benchmark results are not rows because they measure downstream task scores rather than representational convergence.
record.test_reason: Besides proposing a fusion method, the paper reports held-out alignment diagnostics (Match, CKA, Retrieval@1) after PCA plus orthogonal Procrustes between 15 source LLMs and two host LLMs (Fig. 4). These bear directly on whether one model's representations map onto another's by a simple linear map (V4), using a different method from the originals. They also show metric-dependent values (V6). Downstream fusion scores are not alignment measures.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that task-relevant representations across architectures show approximately orthogonal correspondences in low-dimensional subspaces, giving a geometric interface for capability fusion. They also stress that alignment alone does not guarantee task gains, and that absorption depends on the host, its scale and the layer choice.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses shared, task-specific prompts, PCA subspaces, and orthogonal Procrustes alignment to support capability fusion. It does not test the scale-dependent convergence claim or reproduce the original studies’ convergence recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported alignment values differ by metric and source–host pair. Match scores also vary across weak, medium, and best matched layer-pair conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA plus orthogonal mapping gives larger downstream capability-transfer gains than PCA plus unconstrained linear mapping, PCA only, or no alignment (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometry-preserving (orthogonal) cross-model maps transfer functional capability better than unconstrained linear maps.

fits_no_version.finding: Transfer gains increase from weakly to best-matched layer pairs as held-out Match rises (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-alignment similarity predicts usefulness for cross-model representation injection.

record.problems: The alignment results concern task-relevant language-model representations and use paired shared prompts; the method is not evaluated on unpaired data or image-caption modalities. Alignment scores are reported without uncertainty estimates, and the paper does not measure whether similarity rises with model scale or performance. The paper itself notes that alignment alone does not ensure downstream task improvement.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 reports individual alignment metrics for 15 source models on each of two hosts. To stay concise, individual cells other than the reported means and the ChemDFM examples were not extracted; the omitted source-pair results are in Section 3.1, Figure 4.

untested.parts: Whether alignment rises with model scale or capability. Host-scale experiments report only fusion capacity and task gains, not alignment.
All of it; no vision or image-caption data.
All of it; no same-architecture seed comparisons of representations.
Stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, full-dimensional (non-PCA) maps, and alignment between genuinely independent models free of shared base lineage.
All of it; no neuron, SAE or circuit analysis.
Metric settings such as neighbour count, out-of-distribution inputs, and pre- versus post-alignment comparisons.
Plateau, and whether shared data or lineage explains the alignment. Not tested, though the lineage confound is visible.

record.verdict_notes: Fig. 4's source list differs from the appendix's Table 7. Fig. 4 includes Instruction-3B, Math-3B, Code-3B and Safety-3B, which are Llama-3.2-3B MergeBench fine-tunes. This makes the Llama-host scores close to self-comparison, and likely explains why Llama means exceed Qwen means. Alignment is fit per source on domain-specific anchor prompts with a disjoint validation set; no uncertainty is reported for alignment scores. Fig. 3's before/after comparison is qualitative only.

versions.untested_parts: Whether representation alignment increases with model size or capability; whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, and data converge more as they scale.
Cross-modal image-caption representation alignment and whether it rises with vision- and language-model capability.
Convergence across random initializations, shared features or subspaces across seeds, and whether individual units or bases differ.

The study tests orthogonal mapping of paired, task-relevant representations in low-dimensional subspaces. It does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired-data mapping, or whether a map works broadly across tasks without task-specific anchor prompts.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits, including neurons or SAE features, across models.

The study compares several alignment metrics and layer-pair conditions, but does not systematically vary metric settings such as neighbour count, test out-of-distribution inputs, or show that alignment vanishes under other input choices.
Whether alignment plateaus or remains far from complete, and whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment rather than a common model of reality.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.2-3B host, where many sources share Llama lineage or are fine-tunes of the host
relationships.reason: High means (0.90/0.98/0.97, R1-R3) are inflated by shared base models, not independent training. No pre-alignment baseline is given.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Llama-3.2-3B host, where many sources share Llama lineage or are fine-tunes of the host
source_check.reason: R1-R3 show strong mapping correspondence in this tested setting. Shared lineage and missing baselines constrain interpretation but do not demonstrate weaker or failed interchangeability; V4 does not require independent training. The paper does not establish that shared lineage inflated these means.
